'''Desmond John Tobin''' is an Irish academic, researcher and author. He is a full professor of dermatological science at [[University College Dublin]] and the director of the Charles Institute of Dermatology. He was chair of British Society for Investigative Dermatology from 2018 to 2020.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bsid.org.uk/committee/|title=Committee Members}}</ref> Tobin is a fellow of The [[Royal College of Pathologists]], of the [[Higher Education Academy]], of the [[Royal Society of Biology]], [[Institute of Biomedical Science]], and of the Institute of Trichologists (where he is currently vice-president).<ref>{{cite web|title=The Institute of Trichologists - Key Personnel|date=25 May 2020 |url=https://www.trichologists.org.uk/about-us/key-personnel/}}</ref>

Tobin's research is focused on [[pigmentation]] and hair follicle health. He has conducted extensive research on [[Alopecia areata]], where he was the first researcher to show that patients with AA have circulating antibodies to hair follicle-specific antigens, including [[trichohyalin]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=w1B3oX8AAAAJ&hl=en|title=Desmond Tobin - Google Scholar}}</ref> He is also a regional editor for the [[International Journal of Trichology]].

== Education ==
A native of [[Navan]], [[County Meath]], Ireland, Tobin completed high school education at St Patrick’s Classical School, Navan, and was awarded a B.Sc. from [[Maynooth University]] in 1986.{{citation needed|date=December 2021}}

Tobin then joined [[North East Surrey College of Technology]] where he completed his G.I. in Biology (immunology) in 1987. In 1991, he received his Ph.D. from St John's Institute of Dermatology at [[King's College London]]. Subsequently he moved to the [[United States]], where he completed his research post-doctoral training at the Dept. of Dermatology NYU, New York.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://people.ucd.ie/desmond.tobin|title=Desmond Tobin}}</ref>

== Career ==
Tobin briefly worked as Assistant Research Professor at the Department of Dermatology, [[New York University]] and Adjunct Assistant Professor at [[City University of New York]] before moving back to the [[Europe]] in 1996. There he joined [[University of Bradford]] as a lecturer in Biomedical Sciences. He moved up in the ranks becoming a Full Professor in 2004. From 2005 to 2008, he served as the director of the Medical Biosciences Research Group. In 2008, he was appointed the Associate Dean for Research and Knowledge Transfer at the Faculty of Life Sciences.<ref name=UCD/>

Tobin founded the Center for Skin Sciences at University of Bradford in 2009 and served as its director until 2018. In 2018, he left University of Bradford to return home to Ireland to join the University College Dublin, where he was appointed the director of Charles Institute of Dermatology.<ref name=UCD>{{cite web|url=https://www.ucd.ie/medicine/news/may2018/title,410384,en.html|title=New Director at UCD Charles Institute}}</ref>

In 2018, Tobin was appointed the chair of British Society for Investigative Dermatology. In May 2021, he was made a member of the [[Royal Irish Academy]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.ria.ie/news/membership/admittance-day-2021 |title=Admittance Day 2021 |work=Royal Irish Academy |date=21 May 2021 |access-date=2021-05-26}}</ref>

== Research and work ==
=== Pigmentation & neuroendocrine research ===
Tobin’s lab developed an assay for tracking melanin transfer events, followed by a study on a key motor protein to drive melanin transfer between [[melanocyte]]s and [[keratinocyte]]s in human skin.<ref>{{cite journal|url=|title=Hair Follicle Pigmentation|date=2005 |doi=10.1111/j.0022-202X.2004.23528.x |last1=Slominski |first1=Andrzej |last2=Wortsman |first2=Jacobo |last3=Plonka |first3=Przemyslaw M. |last4=Schallreuter |first4=Karin U. |last5=Paus |first5=Ralf |last6=Tobin |first6=Desmond J. |journal=Journal of Investigative Dermatology |volume=124 |pages=13–21 |pmid=15654948 |pmc=1201498 }}</ref> These latter findings were translated in product development for pigmentation spots and potentially also melasma. Via university-owned IP, his team discovered a potential new ‘sun-less tanning’ small peptide technology.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bradford.ac.uk/business/ip/upregulation-of--skin-melanin-content/|title=Upregulation of the melanin content of the skin}}</ref>

Tobin identified the basis for the clinically-observed preferential targeting of pigmented hair (and relative sparing of white hair) in [[Alopecia areata]] (AA), with his data showing that pigmented hair follicle melanocytes are destroyed in acute AA. This also explains rapid so-called ‘going white overnight’.<ref>{{cite web|title=The Fate of Hair Follicle Melanocytes During The Hair Growth Cycle|url=https://www.researchgate.net/publication/12641790}}</ref> Tobin's laboratory was the first to report that the opioid b-endorphin acts a surprising and potent pigmentary molecule.<ref>{{cite journal|url=|title=β-Endorphin: The Forgotten Hair Follicle Melanotropin|date=2005 |doi=10.1111/j.1087-0024.2005.10108.x |last1=Tobin |first1=Desmond J. |last2=Kauser |first2=Söbia |journal=Journal of Investigative Dermatology Symposium Proceedings |volume=10 |issue=3 |pages=212–216 |pmid=16382667 |doi-access=free }}</ref>

Tobin’s work is also interested in the life and death of pigment cells; key not only for those with age-related loss of hair pigmentation, but also for those with malignant pigment cells. He reported the first recognized spontaneous and cyclical programmed cell death in the melanocyte system in humans, during the regression phase of the hair growth cycle. This may be harnessed in apoptosis-resistant melanoma.<ref>Tobin, D. J., Hagen, E., Botchkarev, V. A., &amp; Paus, R. (1998). Do Hair Bulb Melanocytes Undergo Apotosis During Hair Follicle Regression (Catagen)? Journal of Investigative Dermatology, 111(6), 941-947. doi:10.1046/j.1523-1747.1998.00417.x</ref> With vitiligo, he and his colleagues challenged the prevailing view that all melanocytes were lost/destroyed in epidermis of patients with this skin-depigmenting disorder. He proposed that these cells survived best if un/dedifferentiated, opening up possibilities of treating even fully-white vitiligo skin of long duration.<ref>{{cite journal|title=Melanocytes Are Not Absent in Lesional Skin of Long Duration Vitiligo|year=2000|pmid=10918216|last1=Tobin|first1=D. J.|last2=Swanson|first2=N. N.|last3=Pittelkow|first3=M. R.|last4=Peters|first4=E. M.|last5=Schallreuter|first5=K. U.|author-link5=Karin Schallreuter|journal=The Journal of Pathology|volume=191|issue=4|pages=407–16|doi=10.1002/1096-9896(2000)9999:9999<::AID-PATH659>3.0.CO;2-D|s2cid=222087911 }}</ref>

=== Hair follicle in health & disease ===
Tobin with others has assessed the genetics of hair traits, and revealed several novel genes including the first gene associated with gray hair, in addition to other hair traits like mono-brow,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.thetelegraphandargus.co.uk/news/14312604.bradford-scientists-step-closer-to-halting-grey-hair/|title= Bradford scientists 'step closer to halting grey hair'|date= March 2016}}</ref> beard density, and straight vs curly hair.<ref>{{cite journal|title=The biology of hair diversity|year=2013|doi=10.1111/ics.12041|last1=Westgate|first1=Gillian E.|last2=Botchkareva|first2=Natalia V.|last3=Tobin|first3=Desmond J.|journal=International Journal of Cosmetic Science|volume=35|issue=4|pages=329–336|pmid=23363384|s2cid=31518348|doi-access=free}}</ref> He has also advanced the understanding of how [[oxidative stress]] can weaken the melanocyte system of both the skin and aging hair follicle, and how this may be stabilized via anti-oxidant protection.<ref>{{cite journal|title=Aging of the Hair Follicle Pigmentation System|year=2009|pmc=2938584|last1=Tobin|first1=D. J.|journal=International Journal of Trichology|volume=1|issue=2|pages=83–93|doi=10.4103/0974-7753.58550|pmid=20927229 |doi-access=free }}</ref>

Tobin has conducted extensive research on Alopecia areata (AA). He was the first to show that patients with AA have circulating antibodies to hair follicle-specific antigens, including trichohyalin.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.researchgate.net/publication/45718781|title=Trichohyalin is a Potential Major Autoantigen in Human Alopecia Areata}}</ref>

== Awards and honors ==
*1999 - Fellowship of The Institute of Trichologists (Elected Vice-President 2008)
*2008 - Fellowship of The Royal College of Pathologists
*2008 - Fellowship of The Royal Society of Biology
*2011 - Winner of top award in hair science research awarded by European Hair Research Society (John F Ebling Lectureship)
*2012 - Winner of a top award in pigmentation sciences awarded by Asian Society for Pigmentation Research (John Pawelek Lecturership)
*2017 - Fellowship of the Institute of Biomedical Science
*2021 - Elected Member of the Royal Irish Academy<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.ria.ie/bios/membership/t|title=Royal Irish Academy - Membership}}</ref>
